name: Can you convert a tub to a curbless shower in an older Los Angeles home?

mainEntity.name: Can an older home in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank be converted from a tub to a curbless shower?
mainEntity.text: Can an older home in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank be converted from a tub to a curbless shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curbless shower is possible in many older homes, but it is not a simple swap. The floor often has to be opened and rebuilt so the shower area can slope correctly to the drain without creating a trip hazard or water spill. That can mean adjusting joists, recessing the shower area, or using a linear drain. In older Los Angeles-area houses, the subfloor may be uneven or damaged, which adds labor and may require structural repair before the new shower can be installed. A curbless design is often a good choice for aging-in-place goals and a clean modern look, but it demands strong waterproofing and precise planning. Before committing, homeowners should confirm whether the bathroom dimensions and floor framing can support the design without major reconstruction. A contractor who does these projects regularly should explain the slope, drain type, threshold detail, and waterproofing method so the finished shower performs well and does not leak.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but it usually requires more than a standard tub replacement. A curbless shower often needs floor rebuilding, drain adjustments, slope correction, and careful waterproofing, which makes it more complex and costly than a standard low-curb shower.
